question: In electrolytic refining process, on passing the current impurities settle down, those impurities are known as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**anode mud**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Anode mud:**

 
 
• In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is used as the anode.
 
• During electrolysis, the impure metal dissolves, releasing metal ions into the electrolyte.
 
• Impurities that are less reactive than the metal being refined do not dissolve.
 
• These undissolved impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode.
 
• This accumulated residue of impurities is known as "anode mud."
 
• The composition of anode mud varies depending on the impure metal being refined.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**Cathode mud:**

 
 
• "Cathode mud" is not a standard term used in electrolytic refining.
 
• The cathode is where the pure metal is deposited, not where impurities settle.
 
• The cathode increases in mass as the pure metal is deposited.
 
• The cathode is made of pure metal.
 
• Impurities do not collect at the cathode.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Electrolytic mud:**

 
 
• While the term "electrolytic mud" might seem plausible, "anode mud" is the specific and correct term.
 
• "Electrolytic mud" is not a standard scientific term.
 
• The term anode mud is used to specifically describe the sludge from the anode.
 
• The electrolyte itself is a solution, not mud.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Gangue:**

 
 
• Gangue refers to the unwanted rock and mineral matter associated with valuable minerals in an ore.
 
• It is a term used in mining and ore processing, not specifically in electrolytic refining.
 
• Gangue is removed before the electrolytic refining process.
 
• Gangue is associated with raw ore.
 
• Gangue is not related to the electrolytic process itself.
